EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development in the past 24 hours is the significant escalation in rhetoric and potential for renewed military action between the US and Iran, following President Trump's rejection of Iran's latest proposal as "garbage" and his consideration of resuming broader military operations against Iran, including "Project Freedom" in the Strait of Hormuz. Concurrently, Israeli forces executed a major ground operation in southern Lebanon, signaling a heightened conflict beyond established front lines, while Hezbollah escalated its offensive with drones and rockets.

IRAN
Military operations against Iran included a reported covert attack by the UAE on the Lavan Island oil refinery in early April, leading to a large fire and multi-month shutdown. An oil tanker, previously named Sanandaj (Class S), was reportedly hit near Jask overnight, with crew reported safe. Iran has threatened to enrich uranium to 90% if attacked again, and stated its armed forces are ready for a "decisive and crushing" response to any new aggression. Iran's IRGC Navy announced an expansion of the Strait of Hormuz operational zone to a 500-kilometer "crescent," extending from Jask and Sirik to beyond Greater Tunb Island, and claimed to have forced a US warship to change course after a warning. Internally, Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf emphasized readiness for all options and rejection of the US 14-point proposal. The economic situation is strained, with reports of drug shortages (Warfarin, Methimazole, Metformin, Insulin) due to sanctions and supply chain issues, and a crisis in the automobile industry from controlled pricing. The US Treasury found Iran's diplomatic proposal "politically unacceptable" and inconsistent with sanction lifting standards. Internet access continues to be restricted, with "Internet Pro" services criticized as creating a two-tiered system. An individual was executed for alleged involvement in Sunni Baloch terrorism, and another was reportedly executed for spying for the CIA and Mossad.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations were significant, with IDF ground forces completing a week-long raid beyond the Litani River in southern Lebanon, specifically in the Zawtar al-Sharqiyah area, eliminating "dozens" of Hezbollah operatives, locating tunnels and weapon depots, and carrying out over 100 airstrikes. This operation, led by the Golani Brigade’s Reconnaissance Unit, achieved "operational control" over the area, with several Israeli soldiers sustaining light injuries. Since the ceasefire understandings, the IDF reports killing over 350 Hezbollah terrorists and striking more than 1,100 targets in southern Lebanon. In Gaza, the 252nd and 143rd Divisions killed at least four Palestinian terrorists involved in suspicious activities. On the home front, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) launched from the east (suspected Yemen) was intercepted near Eilat. A surface-to-air missile (SAM) fired by Hezbollah at an Israeli Air Force drone over southern Lebanon triggered an interceptor and subsequent sirens in Neve Yam. Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu's court testimony was cut short for urgent security consultations. The Knesset approved a law allowing the death penalty for perpetrators of the October 7th attacks by a majority of 93, with no possibility of release in future hostage deals. The EU approved sanctions against violent Israeli settlers and Hamas figures, a move criticized by Israeli officials as antisemitic. Air India canceled flights to Israel until early July. The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, confirmed Israel sent Iron Dome batteries and personnel to the UAE during the Iran war.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, Israeli forces from the 252nd and 143rd Divisions engaged and killed at least four Palestinian terrorists who posed immediate threats to troops yesterday. The humanitarian situation in Gaza was not explicitly detailed in the provided intelligence. In the West Bank, the EU approved sanctions against "violent settlers" and "senior Hamas figures." Israeli settlers were reported to have targeted Palestinian vehicles on the Nablus-Ramallah road. Israeli occupation forces demolished over 30 Palestinian shops in Al-Eizariya. The military court convicted Nazmi Abu Bakr for the intentional killing of Sgt. First Class Amit Ben Yigal in Ya'bad in 2020.

LEBANON
Hezbollah escalated its operations, firing surface-to-air missiles at Israeli drones (one failed), launching multiple explosive drones (two striking unmanned engineering vehicles and causing damage), and rockets at IDF positions in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah claimed 20 operations on Monday, including destroying a Merkava tank, two D9 armored bulldozers, a Humvee, several engineering vehicles, and fuel tankers in Rashaf, Naqoura, and Tayr Harfa. They also reported multi-stage strikes on Israeli forces in Taybeh and a newly established command center in Biada. Israeli forces conducted airstrikes in Kfar Abba (Nabatieh), Dir Qanoun al-Ras al-Ain (Tyre district), al-Rihan, and Sahmar (Bekaa), and killed two operatives in a vehicle in al-Dawwir. The IDF warned residents of Arzoun, Tyre Daba, Al-Bazoria, and Al-Housh to evacuate. Hezbollah's Secretary-General Naim Qassem stated that the issue of Hezbollah's weapons is not part of negotiations with the "enemy" and that they would not return to the conditions prior to March 2.

SYRIA & IRAQ
IRGC Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani reportedly visited Baghdad in the last two days. The Iraqi-Iranian Supreme Security Committee held a meeting in Baghdad to enhance joint security coordination and border control. Residents in Baghdad reported unidentified warplanes flying over the Rusafa side, causing concern. US Central Command is conducting 24-hour reconnaissance over areas in Anbar province (Nukhaib, Razzaza, Khaldiyah, Kilo 106, H3 line, Tash, Ain Tamar, Wadi Shan'an), considered strategic security risks by Israel. Lebanon exempted Iraqis from financial and legal consequences for overstaying their visas until 31/12/2026. German police in Hamburg arrested a 17-year-old Syrian suspected of planning an ISIS terror attack.

GULF STATES
The UAE reportedly conducted "covert" attacks against Iran, including an attack on the Lavan Island oil refinery in early April. Israel has sent Iron Dome batteries and personnel to the UAE. Kuwait's Interior Ministry announced the arrest of four armed individuals linked to the IRGC who attempted to infiltrate by sea, with one Kuwaiti security force member injured. Qatar requested ships in its main LNG export facility (Ras Laffan) to turn off their Automatic Identification Systems (AIS). The IRGC Navy claimed to have forced a US warship to change course in the Strait of Hormuz. Qatari Foreign Minister discussed regional stability and the Iran-US ceasefire with the Turkish Foreign Minister. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser stated that even if the Strait of Hormuz opens today, it would take months for the market to rebalance. Bahraini citizens were reported to be clashing with authorities over support for the Islamic Republic. Trump criticized Iran for attacking Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE, stating no one expected it.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1. **Renewed US-Iran Escalation**: President Trump rejected Iran's latest peace proposal as "garbage" and is considering two options: resuming "Project Freedom" to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or conducting broader bombing campaigns against 25% of identified targets in Iran.
2. **UAE Covert Attacks & Israeli Support**: The UAE secretly carried out attacks against Iran, including the Lavan Island oil refinery in early April, and Israel confirmed sending Iron Dome batteries and personnel to the UAE.
3. **Iran's Nuclear Threat & Hormuz Stance**: Iran threatened to enrich uranium to 90% if attacked, and the IRGC Navy declared an expanded, 500km operational "crescent" in the Strait of Hormuz, asserting full control.
4. **Major Israeli Ground Operation in Lebanon**: IDF's Golani Brigade completed a week-long raid beyond the Litani River in southern Lebanon (Zawtar al-Sharqiyah), neutralizing dozens of Hezbollah operatives and infrastructure, with several Israeli soldiers lightly injured.
5. **Hezbollah Offensive Actions**: Hezbollah escalated its attacks in southern Lebanon, launching explosive drones (damaging two Israeli engineering vehicles), rockets, and a failed SAM launch, and claiming 20 operations against Israeli targets on Monday.
6. **Kuwaiti Interception of IRGC Infiltrators**: Kuwaiti authorities arrested four armed individuals linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards attempting to infiltrate Kuwait by sea.
7. **EU Sanctions on Israeli Settlers**: The European Union agreed to impose sanctions against "violent settlers" in the West Bank and senior Hamas figures.
8. **Israeli Death Penalty Law**: The Knesset passed a law enabling the death penalty for perpetrators of the October 7th attacks.
9. **Pakistan & Turkey Mediation Efforts**: Pakistan continues high-level diplomatic contacts and mediation efforts between the US and Iran, particularly concerning the opening of the Strait of Hormuz, with Turkey also playing a role.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are extremely high. President Trump's consideration of renewed military action against Iran, including the "Project Freedom" operation in the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with Iran's explicit threat to enrich uranium to 90% if attacked, creates an immediate and severe flashpoint. The Strait of Hormuz is an active flashpoint, with reported GPS disruptions, IRGC Navy expansion of its operational definition, and a US nuclear submarine (USS Alaska) confirmed in the region. Southern Lebanon remains a highly active conflict zone due to the ongoing IDF ground operations beyond the Litani River and intensified Hezbollah rocket and drone attacks. The covert actions by the UAE against Iran and Israel's deployment of Iron Dome to the UAE indicate a broadening regional involvement and potential for further Iranian retaliation against Gulf states.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** stance is hardening, with President Trump rejecting Iran's latest proposal, considering renewed military action, and announcing a meeting with top generals on Iran. He also stated disappointment with the Kurds for not delivering weapons into Iran and launched investigations into media leaks about the war. The **Gulf States** are directly involved, with the UAE's covert attacks on Iran and Israel's Iron Dome deployment to the Emirates. Qatar is coordinating with Gulf partners and mediating with Turkey on the Iran-US ceasefire. Kuwait arrested IRGC-linked infiltrators. **EU members** agreed to sanctions against "violent settlers" in the West Bank and Hamas figures, a move welcomed by France. The UK Prime Minister, Keir Starmer, reiterated he would not drag Britain into the Iran war, although the UK imposed sanctions on 12 individuals and entities linked to Iran. **Russia** announced Putin's visit to China, the end of the humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine, and denied CNN reports of a sunken ship carrying nuclear components for North Korea. Russia is also reported to be expanding a drone factory and supplying parts to Iran. **China** expressed opposition to US sanctions on its companies related to Iran and will host Putin for talks that include Iran. **Turkey's** Foreign Minister Fidan is actively mediating between the US and Iran, emphasizing a diplomatic solution and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. **Pakistan** is also engaged in high-level diplomatic contacts to mediate the conflict and secure the opening of the Strait of Hormuz, although it denied reports of sheltering Iranian military aircraft.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims were noted. The Iraqi security forces denied the existence of any unauthorized bases or an Israeli airstrip in Anbar, contrasting with Faytuks Network's claim of uncovering one. Pakistan's Foreign Ministry explicitly denied CBS News reports that it sheltered Iranian military aircraft at Nur Khan Air Force Base following the ceasefire. Iranian sources from Tasnim denied any agreement to move enriched uranium out of Iran, while other Iranian reports implied an agreement to dilute uranium under IAEA supervision. Trump's claim that Iran lacks the technology to remove "nuclear dust" from destroyed facilities remains unverified by independent sources. Statements from the Iranian government spokesperson regarding "Internet Pro" being for businesses contradict numerous citizen reports of unsolicited activations for private users. Hezbollah's claims of destroying multiple Israeli military assets are not fully corroborated by IDF reports, which mentioned damage to unmanned engineering vehicles but no casualties to personnel in specific incidents. Reporting gaps exist regarding the exact number of Hezbollah casualties in the Litani operation (stated as "dozens") and the full extent of damage to the oil tanker reportedly hit near Jask. The incident of unidentified warplanes over Baghdad needs further investigation. The "omid dana" channel frequently publishes unverified, highly inflammatory, and anti-regime claims (e.g., Trump's intent to "end the regime," Qazvin explosions, specific attack dates), which are indicative of propaganda and should be treated with extreme caution. Press TV similarly displays strong pro-Iranian regime and anti-Western/Israeli biases in its reporting.
